anchor_text: <Dialogue speaker="SPEAKER_02" time="01:13:50">Yeah, it's not like there's a certain number of times you have to do it.</Dialogue>

<Dialogue speaker="SPEAKER_03" time="01:47:01">Can you hear me, Father? Yes, we hear you. Welcome. Welcome. I'm just one of those people who called in just to say, but was missed in the second half. Okay. No, actually, the question actually came up in the, this end of the second half in regards to the offering of incense and how that relates to the sacrificial system. So it's been reiterated. Multiple times that a sacrifice is a meal that's consumed. Incense seems to be an interesting place. I'm not aware of anywhere in the Old Testament that incense is used as a sin offering. But at the very least, the pagans tried to force Christians to offer incense sacrifices to the gods, even though incense isn't. It's quite a meal. But also, we have the incense that we will send the icons with, and we see that as something different than the sacrifice of the [[Eucharist]]. So what the heck is going on with incense and sacrifice?</Dialogue>
